You are a strategic innovation advisor. Analyse the company profile and questionnaire responses, then respond ONLY with valid JSON in this exact format:
{"maturity_score": <float 0-10>, "opportunities": [{"id": "<unique id e.g. opp_1>", "type": "incremental or radical", "title": "<string>", "rationale": "<string>", "execution_plan": {"first_actions": ["<specific, concrete first steps>"], "resources_needed": ["<specific tools, budget range, headcount, skills>"], "success_metric": "<measurable KPI with target number>", "milestones": ["<concrete milestone with timing>"]}, "impact": "low, medium or high", "difficulty": "low, medium or high", "timeframe": "<string>"}], "next_steps": [{"id": "<unique id e.g. step_1>", "action": "<specific action>", "owner": "<role>", "timeframe": "<e.g. Within 2 weeks>"}], "key_weaknesses": ["<string>"]}

Consider the following when forming your assessment:
- Estimated annual innovation budget: ~€2,250,000/year (3% of €50M+ revenue). Decision-making structure (varies_by_project) should directly influence the "difficulty" and "timeframe" values, as well as the concreteness of "resources_needed" in execution_plan. When estimating resources_needed (e.g. tools, headcount, consulting spend), stay within the realistic bounds of the estimated budget above. Low budget or single-owner approval should bias toward lower-difficulty, faster-timeframe opportunities with minimal resource asks unless justified otherwise.
- Customer feedback process (informal_conversations) should influence whether opportunities lean toward validated, incremental improvements or exploratory, radical bets.
- Regulatory environment (medium) should directly influence "difficulty" and "timeframe": high regulation should push toward higher difficulty, longer timeframes, and "first_actions" that explicitly include compliance, legal review, or certification steps where relevant. Low regulation allows faster, more experimental timeframes without added compliance overhead.
- Competitive pressure (medium) should influence the balance between "incremental" and "radical" opportunity types: high urgency should bias toward including at least one radical, faster-moving opportunity even if higher risk, while low urgency justifies purely incremental, longer-horizon suggestions. Explicitly reflect this urgency in the "rationale" field when relevant.
- Risk appetite (conservative) should be the primary driver of the "type" field for each opportunity: "conservative" should produce mostly or entirely "incremental" opportunities with cautious framing in the rationale; "bold" should include at least one clearly "radical" opportunity even if difficulty is high; "balanced" should mix both types roughly evenly. Do not contradict a conservative risk appetite with a majority-radical opportunity list, even if competitive pressure is high — in that case, favor faster-timeframe incremental moves instead.
- Strategic priority (growth) should shape the "title" and "rationale" of each opportunity so they visibly serve that priority: "growth" opportunities should target new revenue, customers or markets; "efficiency" opportunities should target cost reduction or process optimization; "market_defense" opportunities should target retention, competitive moats or countering specific competitor moves; "diversification" opportunities should target new products, verticals or business models distinct from the core business.
- Tailoring: every opportunity and next step must reference the company's ACTUAL sector, product, or market (from the Company description and Sector above) — never generic SaaS/tech playbook advice. Name the company's real product category, customer type, or competitive context.

CRITICAL REQUIREMENTS FOR EXECUTION PLANS:
- "first_actions" must be concrete and immediately actionable — name specific tools, roles, or deliverables. Avoid vague phrases like "establish a process" or "conduct analysis" without specifying what the process/analysis actually involves.
- "success_metric" must include a measurable BASELINE AND TARGET with numbers (e.g. "increase customer retention from 92% to 96%"), never a bare "improve by 15%" without a baseline.
- "milestones" must include rough time markers (e.g. "Month 1", "Quarter 2") so the plan reads as a real roadmap, not a wishlist.
- Every "next_steps" item must specify who is responsible and a realistic timeframe — not just what should happen.
- "resources_needed" must state an explicit euro amount for EVERY resource — either a one-off figure or an annual figure (e.g. "€5,000 one-off", "€40,000/year for 1 part-time project manager"). These figures must be a plausible fraction of the estimated innovation budget above. NEVER write vague costs like "low-cost tool", "some consulting", or "10 hours of staff time" without a concrete € figure.
- Every opportunity MUST include ALL execution_plan fields: first_actions, resources_needed, success_metric, and milestones. Do not omit any field.

Here is ONE illustrative example of the level of concreteness, euro-anchoring, and sector-tailoring expected. DO NOT copy it — tailor every detail to the actual company above:

{"id": "opp_1", "type": "incremental", "title": "Automated inventory reordering for the top 50 SKUs", "rationale": "The company is a mid-size wholesale distributor with a lean operations team; automating reorder points on its fastest-moving SKUs cuts stockout losses and frees the two warehouse staff for higher-value work.", "execution_plan": {"first_actions": ["Extract 12 months of SKU-level sales history from the existing ERP (Sage 200)", "Define min/max reorder thresholds for the top 50 SKUs with the warehouse supervisor", "Enable the built-in reorder module in the current ERP rather than buying a new tool"], "resources_needed": ["ERP reorder module licence: €3,000/year", "0.25 FTE operations analyst: €11,000/year", "ERP consultant configuration: €2,400 one-off"], "success_metric": "Reduce stockout incidents from 14 per quarter to 4 per quarter within 6 months", "milestones": ["Month 1: SKU history extracted and thresholds defined", "Month 2: ERP reorder module configured and tested", "Month 4: Live on all 50 SKUs, first stockout report reviewed"]}, "impact": "high", "difficulty": "medium", "timeframe": "6 months"}

Provide 3 prioritized opportunities, 3 next steps, and 3 key_weaknesses.
Write a 2-3 sentence rationale for each opportunity that connects it to the company's actual sector, strategy, and constraints — not a generic statement.
Each next step must be 2-3 sentences: explain the strategic rationale, the concrete action, a specific named owner, and a precise timeframe.

IMPORTANT: Respond with a single valid JSON object only. No markdown, no explanation, no extra text.
Output COMPACT JSON — minimize line breaks and indentation to maximize content density.
Use the exact key "execution_plan" (not variations) and always include "type" for every opportunity.
Ensure all arrays are closed with ] and the object is closed with }.

Company: Nova
Sector: Arts, Entertainment & Media
Size: Medium

Company Description: Nova is a specialized music rights and publishing entity managing an extensive catalog of 5,000 songs spanning various genres. The company handles complex royalty collection across multiple territories, manages sync licensing for film and advertising, and maintains strict copyright enforcement protocols. While the core operations are stable, significant friction exists between legacy manual tracking systems and the rapidly evolving demands of digital streaming platforms.

Innovation Process: informal
Digital Maturity: 2/4
Customer Feedback: informal_conversations

Strategic Goals: Targeting 30% year-over-year top-line growth. We see untapped demand in adjacent customer segments like direct-to-consumer fan engagement tools and are evaluating whether to build, buy, or partner to accelerate market penetration into these areas. The core question is whether to deepen our vertical specialization in high-value sync licensing or broaden horizontally into related product categories.
Strategic Priority: growth
Time Horizon: medium
Risk Appetite: conservative

Team Size: We have a dedicated innovation squad of 8 people — 4 engineers, 1 data scientist, 1 UX designer, 1 product manager, and a part-time business analyst. This team operates with its own sprint cadence separate from the core product teams and has an allocated annual innovation budget. They report progress quarterly to the executive committee.
Revenue Range: over_50m
Estimated Innovation Budget: ~€2,250,000/year (3% of €50M+ revenue)
Decision Making: varies_by_project

Main Barriers: culture, talent, time
Competitive Pressure: medium
Regulatory Environment: medium

Past Initiatives: We experimented with a customer self-service portal two years ago after seeing competitors offer similar functionality but failed to achieve meaningful adoption due to a lack of deep market insight. We built an MVP for AI similarity detection internally in 3 months, which proved technically feasible but lacked the necessary data pipeline integration and operational support for real-time infringement monitoring.
Additional Context: The company is currently balancing the need to modernize aging back-end financial systems with the urgent requirement for scalable data infrastructure needed to support future AI-driven revenue forecasting.
